question: can we keep 4 encoders but have something LEARNED (projection or distilled student) and still have the codebook?

Distillation.recommendation: Run multi-teacher distillation as a PRE-REGISTERED CONTROL ARM against config B's fixed random projection, not as a replacement for it. Concretely: (0) precondition, no training — compute the four encoders' activation statistics (global and per-channel mean/std) and RankMe on the 20,413 frames; PHI-S shows this determines whether loss balancing is even possible, and if the scales differ by orders of magnitude (as their DFN-CLIP global std 0.0049-0.0286 vs SAM 1.1475-5.4688 did) then standardized targets are mandatory rather than optional. (1) Cache final-layer teacher targets, K=4 augmented views, fp16 = ~156 GB; do NOT cache all 88 layers (1,047 GB, and 88 per-layer heads is ~265M head params on a ViT-B, more head than backbone) — if depth must be preserved, distil 3 depth groups per teacher (12 heads) matching the existing shallow/mid/deep factorisation. Caching is load-bearing: it turns the DUNE examples-seen-equivalent schedule (6,276 epochs over IMPACT) from 1,050 GPU-hours of live 4-teacher forwards into ~70. (2) Student = ViT-B/16 768-d initialized from USFM or USF-MAE (already ultrasound ViT-B/16, same grid, in-domain init); ViT-S is 10.7x compression against the 4,096-d teacher union, ViT-L at 64 targets/param is over-capacity for 20k images. (3) Loss = RADIO-style per-teacher 2-layer MLP heads (hidden = 1536 = max teacher dim), cosine + smooth-L1 on spatial features, teachers equally weighted AFTER target standardization, bilinear interpolation UP to 16x16 (not config B's downsample to 14x14), UNIC-style teacher dropping as the balancing regularizer. (4) 1,000-3,000 cached epochs = 11-33 GPU-hours; patience is cheap once teachers are cached. (5) Gate on the pre-set D1-D8 thresholds BEFORE stage 2; if any fails, stop and report a characterized null — do not tune to pass. (6) Stage 2: freeze the student, run the existing EMA VQ (K=256, dead-code reinit) on trunk-concat-heads, evaluate under the project's fixed protocol (GroupKFold-by-fetus with PER-FOLD student refit for the headline, >=2000-bootstrap CI against config B as the matched-capacity baseline, label-shuffle permutation, PE maternal negative control, scanner/plane/GA/image-count adjustment). The single thing this buys that a random projection cannot is per-teacher decodability: a shared code pushed through each frozen head yields that teacher's NATIVE features, so 'what does this code mean in FetalCLIP's terms' becomes a computation rather than an inference from a random 256-d shadow. Expected GA r from the codes is 0.33-0.42 against the current 0.385 — plausibly a wash — and either outcome is publishable, because 'a learned four-teacher student does not improve the discrete vocabulary over a fixed random projection, and here is the rank/fidelity evidence it did not collapse' answers the design question the paper must address anyway.
Distillation.mechanism: TWO STAGES, student frozen for stage 2. STAGE 1 (distillation): the four encoders stay FROZEN and are never fine-tuned. Learned = one student ViT-B/16 (768-d, 16x16 grid, initialized from USFM or USF-MAE) plus one 2-layer MLP projection head per teacher (LayerNorm+GELU between; in=768, hidden=1536=max teacher dim, out=that teacher's dim: 1024/768/768/1536). Critically the mapping direction is INVERTED relative to config B: config B projects the TEACHERS down into a shared random 256-d space; here the STUDENT is projected OUT to each teacher's own native space, exactly as AM-RADIO does, so no common space is ever imposed and no teacher information is discarded by a shared bottleneck. Loss = sum over teachers of [cosine distance + smooth-L1] between head_i(student_spatial(x)) and teacher_i_spatial(x), with the teacher targets STANDARDIZED (PHI-S-style, invertibly) before the loss so that unequal activation scales do not silently become a teacher-weighting scheme; teachers equally weighted (RADIO's gamma_i=1 default) after standardization; grid mismatch resolved by bilinear interpolation UP to the larger resolution (16x16), following RADIO; UNIC-style teacher dropping as the only balancing regularizer. NO OUTCOME LABEL ENTERS STAGE 1 — no GA, SGA, birth percentile, PE, or NICU. Teacher targets are cached (teachers frozen => outputs are constants), K=4 augmented views per image, fp16, ~156 GB for final-layer targets. STAGE 2 (vocabulary): the student and heads are FROZEN. The existing EMA codebook with dead-code reinit (the machinery that already achieves 256/256 codes used, where a gradient codebook collapsed to 9/32) is fit on the concatenation of the student trunk features and its four head outputs — quantising trunk-plus-heads rather than the trunk alone is what preserves config B's shared/private decomposition inside the distilled design. Reconstruction MSE in stage 2 therefore measures fidelity against a FIXED target, which is the whole point of separating the stages.
Distillation.circularity_analysis: SPLIT THE QUESTION. (A) OUTCOME CIRCULARITY: absent. No outcome label — GA, SGA, birth percentile, PE, NICU — enters the student's loss. The teachers stay frozen and nothing is fine-tuned on GA, so the project's cardinal trap (define an axis via the outcome it is then tested against) is untouched. The distillation objective is label-free by construction, which is precisely why the agglomerative literature calls it label-free multi-teacher distillation. (B) CHANGE OF REFERENT: present, and it is the real cost. After distillation the codebook describes S(x) — the student's best 20k-image, four-teacher-consensus approximation of fetal ultrasound — not the teachers and not the images. Config B has the same problem in a different place (its codebook describes a fixed random 256-d shadow of the teachers), but config B's map is DATA-INDEPENDENT: it cannot have absorbed cohort idiosyncrasy because it never saw the cohort. A learned student can. That is the price of 'learned' and it is not zero. The interpretability claim therefore SURVIVES, but only in a narrowed and explicitly stated form, and only if it is defended with evidence rather than asserted. Four measurable conditions would make it NOT survive: (1) student-specific artifacts — codes with no coherent support in any teacher's native feature space (D9, pre-registered allowance <=10% of codes); (2) consensus impoverishment — if the student keeps only the four-teacher intersection, the vocabulary describes the intersection, and this project has already measured that the consensus term carries only ~24% of the reconstructible signal (full recon 0.2984 vs shared-only 0.8297 against ~1.0), so a single shared trunk is exactly the wrong-shaped device unless trunk+heads are quantised together; (3) cohort absorption — if code statistics and teacher-side coherence do not transfer to the clinical set (D10), the vocabulary describes IMPACT's scanners; (4) teacher monopoly — if per-teacher fidelity is grossly unequal (D5), the 'four-encoder vocabulary' framing is false advertising and the codebook describes whichever teacher won. There is also a leakage-flavoured circularity distinct from the outcome kind: the student is fit on the same fetuses whose held-out folds later carry the evaluation, so the headline must come from a per-fold student refit, not an all-data student. Honest framing if this arm ships: 'a discrete vocabulary over the shared content of four frozen ultrasound/vision encoders, as recoverable by a student trained on 20k frames of this cohort' — with the teacher-side coherence audit as the evidence that the words mean something outside the student. Anything broader than that sentence is not supported by what this design can establish.
Distillation.kill_criterion: The arm is dead if EITHER the student collapses — RankMe effective-rank / student-dim < 0.30 on held-out patch tokens (versus 0.606 for SAM-H, the weakest healthy published ViT), or stage-2 reconstruction MSE within 30% of the shuffled-student control at matched VQ capacity — OR it survives non-collapse but buys nothing: codes from the PER-FOLD-REFIT student fail to reach GA r >= 0.33 with a >=2000-bootstrap CI that overlaps config B's 0.385, WHILE >=10% of codes show no coherent support in any teacher's native feature space. The first disjunct kills it for being degenerate; the second kills it for matching neither config B's accuracy nor delivering the per-teacher interpretable meaning that is the only thing distillation offers over a random projection. Either way the result is written up as a characterized null, with the diagnostic values reported, and config B stands.

failure_modes.mode: Student collapse to near-constant / low-rank features that are trivially reconstructible
failure_modes.why_it_happens: 20,413 images (effective n = 908 fetuses, ~22.5 frames each) against a 85.8M-parameter student = 228 scalar targets per parameter at final-layer-only supervision. Under-constrained trunks minimize a standardized regression loss by emitting the per-channel mean plus a small image-dependent perturbation; a codebook then reconstructs that almost perfectly and the recon MSE looks excellent while the representation carries nothing.
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: D1 RankMe effective rank / student dim on HELD-OUT patch tokens: pass >= 0.60 (SAM-H, the weakest healthy published ViT, is 0.606), KILL below 0.30. D2 fraction of channels with across-patch std < 0.01x median channel std: pass < 5%. D3 across-image variance of the mean patch token / mean within-image across-patch variance: pass > 0.15. D4 SHUFFLED-STUDENT CONTROL — refit the same-capacity VQ on student features permuted across images; the real student's recon MSE must be >= 30% better than that control, otherwise the codes describe capacity, not content. D1 catches collapse spectrally, D4 catches it operationally (a constant-ish student reconstructs almost as well after shuffling).
failure_modes.known_fix: Larger effective dataset via the clinical set (30,257 frames) for stage 1; in-domain pretrained init (USFM/USF-MAE) rather than from scratch; PHI-S target standardization so no teacher's scale dominates; spectral reparametrization + weight decay 0.02 (RADIO's own stated remedy against attention entropy collapse); shorten schedule or shrink to ViT-S if D1 degrades over training.

failure_modes.mode: Teacher monopoly — one encoder captures the student and the four-encoder framing becomes false
failure_modes.why_it_happens: Directly observed in the literature, not hypothesized: with AMTML-KD, RADIO reports the model 'would always collapse its entire weight around the CLIP teacher' and performed worse than naive manual balancing. The mechanism is unequal activation scale (PHI-S Table 7: global std ranging 0.0049 to 5.4688 across teachers) — whichever teacher has the largest target variance contributes most of an unnormalized MSE, so the balance is set by an accident of each encoder's output scale. Our four encoders' statistics have never been compared.
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: D5 per-teacher held-out fidelity: R^2 (or 1 - normalized MSE) of head_i(student) against teacher i's true features, computed per teacher. Pass = all four >= 0.50 AND max/min ratio < 2.0. Also D6 kNN agreement: overlap@10 between the student-space and each teacher's NATIVE-space nearest-neighbour graphs on held-out patches, pass > 0.25 for all four (chance ~ 10/N). Both are per-teacher by construction, so a monopoly cannot hide inside an average.
failure_modes.known_fix: PHI-S standardization of the targets (the whole point of that paper); RADIO's naive equal weighting AFTER standardization rather than any learned lambda; UNIC teacher dropping. Explicitly do NOT use AMTML-KD or uncertainty weighting — both are documented to fail or to be metric-dependent (AdaLoss: best on ImageNet, worst on ADE20K).

failure_modes.mode: Consensus impoverishment — the student learns only the four-teacher intersection and destroys the encoder-specific content that this project has already measured to be dominant
failure_modes.why_it_happens: A single student with a shared trunk is structurally a consensus device: the trunk minimizes total loss by encoding what all four teachers want, and encoder-specific content survives only to the extent the per-teacher heads can synthesize it from the trunk. This project has ALREADY measured how expensive that is in the depth-factorised VQ: full recon MSE 0.2984 vs shared(mean)-only 0.8297 against a ~1.0 no-recon baseline, i.e. the consensus term carries only ~24% of the reconstructible signal, and the recorded finding was that depth-specific content dominates.
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: Compare stage-2 recon MSE and code-derived GA r for (a) the trunk alone vs (b) trunk-concat-four-head-outputs, at MATCHED discrete capacity in bits (the project's own recorded caveat is that its 0.366->0.298 flat-vs-factorised comparison was NOT bit-matched — do not repeat that). If the trunk alone loses most of the signal that trunk+heads retains, the trunk is a consensus bottleneck. Second: per-teacher head fidelity D5 measured on the RESIDUAL a teacher's features have after projecting out the other three teachers' predictable content — if residual fidelity is near zero for all four, the student kept only the intersection.
failure_modes.known_fix: Quantise trunk-concat-heads rather than the trunk alone; or carry config B's shared/private structure into the distilled design as private codebooks on the per-teacher head residuals. Increase student width (ViT-B 768-d is already 5.33x compression against the 4,096-d union of teacher final-layer dims). If the effect is severe, this is the argument that a single student is the wrong device for this project and config B should stand.

failure_modes.mode: Cohort absorption — the codebook describes IMPACT's scanners and acquisition rather than fetal anatomy
failure_modes.why_it_happens: This is the intrinsic cost of replacing a data-INDEPENDENT map with a learned one. The fixed random projection cannot absorb cohort idiosyncrasy because it never saw the cohort; a student trained on 20,413 frames from one cohort, one GA window (26-39wk) and a handful of planes can and will. The project has independently measured that imaging PLANE is a strong nuisance axis in this data (NMF factors reached eta^2 = 0.78 on plane).
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: D10 cross-cohort stability: run the FROZEN student on the clinical set (30,257 frames, GA 6.2-41.6wk, different acquisition) and recompute code-usage entropy and per-code teacher-space coherence (D9); pass = no more than 25% relative drop in either. Plus the project's standing confound battery on the code histogram — scanner/plane/dataset/GA/image-count adjustment, and the plane-residual test that config B already passes (95% of GA r survives regressing plane out). If the student's codes lose far more GA r under plane residualization than config B's do, the student absorbed plane.
failure_modes.known_fix: Distil stage 1 on the clinical set as well as IMPACT (relieves diversity, but changes what the codebook describes — a decision for the user, not a detail); scanner/site-balanced sampling; report the arm as cohort-bound if it fails. Note honestly that config B is IMMUNE to this failure by construction, which is a real argument in its favour.

failure_modes.mode: Student-specific vocabulary artifacts — codes that exist only in the student's approximation and correspond to nothing in any teacher
failure_modes.why_it_happens: The referent changes: after distillation the codebook describes S(x), the student's best 20k-image four-teacher-consensus approximation, not the teachers and not the images. Approximation error is not uniform, so the student can carve structure that reflects where its fit is poor rather than where the ultrasound differs.
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: D9 teacher-side code coherence: for every student code, take the patches assigned to it and measure their concentration in each teacher's NATIVE un-projected feature space — mean pairwise cosine within-code vs a random patch set of equal size, per teacher. A code with no teacher-side concentration in any of the four is a student artifact. Pre-register the allowed fraction: pass = >= 90% of codes coherent in at least one teacher.
failure_modes.known_fix: None that removes the artifacts; the fix is disclosure and bounding. Report the artifact fraction as a headline number in the paper, and frame the claim precisely as a vocabulary over the recoverable shared content of four frozen encoders rather than over fetal ultrasound as such.

failure_modes.mode: JOINT-TRAINING target shrinkage — the exact pathology that motivated rejecting a learned projection, now with the codebook as accomplice
failure_modes.why_it_happens: In a joint student+VQ objective the student is simultaneously the thing being quantised and the thing defining the reconstruction target. VQ reconstruction gradient reaches the trunk, and the trunk can lower that loss by making its own output space EASIER to quantise — lower entropy, lower effective rank, clustered near K centroids — instead of encoding more about the image. Recon MSE stops being a fidelity measure because the target moved; the distillation and VQ losses compete for the trunk with no principled lambda (and RADIO already showed automatic balancing collapses onto one term); and 'did the codebook capture fetal structure' becomes unfalsifiable because any residual is explicable as student adaptation.
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: Do not run the joint version — it is disqualified by design, not by measurement. If it is run anyway, the detector is a monotone decline in D1 (RankMe) and in the student's own linear-probe GA r (D8) as the VQ loss weight is increased, while recon MSE improves: representation degrading while the reconstruction number gets better is the signature of target shrinkage. A frozen-student two-stage control is the only reference against which that is legible.
failure_modes.known_fix: Two stages, student frozen for stage 2. Stage 1 has exactly one loss (match frozen teachers, no codebook, no outcome labels); stage 2 quantises a fixed map with already-validated machinery. This breaks the loop cleanly and is the only admissible version.

failure_modes.mode: Stage-1/stage-2 fetus leakage — the student sees the fetuses its codes are later evaluated on
failure_modes.why_it_happens: The classic trap in this exact shape. If stage 1 trains on all 20,413 frames and stage 2 then evaluates code-derived GA/outcome structure by GroupKFold-by-fetus, every fetus in every test fold was in the student's training set. GroupKFold protects the codebook and the probe but not the representation, so it looks like a clean protocol while the representation is fit on the test fetuses.
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: Refit the student PER FOLD (5 students; ~56 GPU-hours cached, affordable) or hold a fetus block out of stage 1 entirely, and report the gap between the fold-refit number and the all-data-student number. A large gap IS the leakage measurement. The fold-refit number is the headline; the all-data number is secondary and labelled as such.
failure_modes.known_fix: Per-fold student refit for the headline, made cheap by caching teacher targets (11 GPU-hours per 1,000-epoch student). Do not report the all-data-student number as the result.

failure_modes.mode: Multiplicity inflation across the arm's configuration space
failure_modes.why_it_happens: This is the n-th representation construction in a project with a long registry of settled nulls. A student adds architecture x init x schedule x loss form x normalization scheme x depth-group count x K to the search space, and each combination is a fresh chance to find a spurious GA/outcome number.
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: Count the constructions x endpoints x windows actually tried and adjust the bar accordingly; the pre-registered configuration in the recommendation is ONE construction. Run the label-shuffle permutation and PE maternal negative control through the identical pipeline (the project's VQ arm already establishes a flat null: all-codes r = -0.006, k=20 combo r = 0.002 under GA shuffle). Any GA r that does not exceed its own shuffle null by more than the bootstrap CI width is within noise.
failure_modes.known_fix: Freeze the entire configuration in a prereg before the first GA number is computed; register this arm against the project's multiplicity budget; report every configuration examined, including the ones abandoned.

key_papers.citation: Ranzinger, Heinrich, Kautz, Molchanov. AM-RADIO: Agglomerative Vision Foundation Model — Reduce All Domains Into One. CVPR 2024.
key_papers.why_relevant: Confirms the user's recollection and supplies the four answers verified from the paper text. (i) Heterogeneous dims: does NOT marginalize teachers into a unified target — maps the student to each teacher independently via teacher-specific 2-layer MLP projection heads (LayerNorm+GELU, hidden = max teacher embed dim), two heads per teacher (summary + spatial). (ii) Grid mismatch: for the spatial loss they 'bilinearly interpolate the outputs to match the larger resolution between the student and teacher features'; where a teacher cannot run at student resolution they run it natively and upsample. (iii) Balancing: cosine + smooth-L1 for spatial features (cosine beat L1/MSE/smooth-L1 on summary; smooth-L1 retained to match vector magnitudes), 'mostly opted toward naive loss balancing' with gamma_i=1; automatic balancing FAILED adversarially — with AMTML-KD 'the model would always collapse its entire weight around the CLIP teacher' and did worse than naive manual balancing. (iv) Beats teachers, but explicitly 'given a student model of sufficient capacity' — at 1.4B DataComp images, batch 1024, 600k steps = 614M examples seen. That precondition is 68,584x our distinct-image count and is why the beats-teachers claim must not be imported.

key_papers.citation: Ranzinger et al. PHI-S: Distribution Balancing for Label-Free Multi-Teacher Distillation. 2024.
key_papers.why_relevant: The load-bearing paper for whether OUR four teachers can be balanced at all. Their Table 7 shows teacher activation statistics differ by orders of magnitude (global std: DFN CLIP 0.0049-0.0286, SigLIP 0.0211-1.8389, DINOv2 0.0055-1.3496, SAM 1.1475-5.4688; SAM per-channel means span -62.03 to +19.17), so an unnormalized MSE IS a teacher-weighting scheme chosen by accident. Their fix standardizes the TARGETS invertibly rather than tuning lambda. Also supplies the collapse-threshold reference used for our diagnostic D1: RankMe effective rank / ambient dim = 0.606 (SAM-H, weakest) to 0.893 (DINOv2-b-reg), with RADIO-class students at 0.84-0.85 — and their observation that teachers are not effectively full rank is the mechanism by which a same-size student can hold several teachers at once. Downsampling SAM features degraded them (they padded and cropped instead), which is direct evidence against config B's resample-everything-down-to-14x14 choice.

key_papers.citation: Sariyildiz, Weinzaepfel, Lucas, Larlus, Kalantidis. UNIC: Universal Classification Models via Multi-teacher Distillation. ECCV 2024.
key_papers.why_relevant: Independent confirmation of the failure direction we most fear, on a MUCH smaller corpus (ImageNet-1K, 1.28M images): with DINO + DeiT-III teachers the multi-teacher student learns faster but CONVERGES LOWER than distilling DeiT-III alone. Their remedy — teacher dropping regularization plus a ladder of expendable projectors — is what I import as the balancing mechanism instead of any automatic lambda scheme.

key_papers.citation: Venkataramanan, Sariyildiz, Larlus, Weinzaepfel, et al. DUNE: Distilling a Universal Encoder from Heterogeneous 2D and 3D Teachers. 2025.
key_papers.why_relevant: The SMALLEST-data agglomerative work I could find, and therefore our nearest precedent: ImageNet-19k, compute fixed at 100x1,281,167 images processed (= 100 IN-1k epochs), distilled at 336x336. Still 686x more distinct images than our 20,413. Two findings I use directly: projector design matters a lot (transformer projector 44.9 vs ladder-of-projectors 42.4 mIoU on ADE20K), and WHICH data you distil on is non-trivial — 'Data associated with a specific teacher can be irrelevant or even harmful to others' — which is the diversity (not count) argument against our single-cohort, single-GA-window corpus. Their headline is measured, not triumphal: 'comparable to that of its larger teachers, sometimes even outperforming them'.

key_papers.citation: Beyer, Zhai, Royer, Markeeva, Anil, Kolesnikov. Knowledge distillation: A good teacher is patient and consistent. CVPR 2022.
key_papers.why_relevant: The ONLY small-data precedent, and the reason the from-scratch ResNet-18 failure does not transfer. They establish function-matching distillation on Flowers102 (1,020 images) and Pets (3,312 images) — 20x and 6x SMALLER than our 20,413 — under two conditions: consistency (student and teacher see the SAME augmented view) and patience (very long schedules; a fixed teacher saturates and overfits while function matching does not). This sets both our schedule prescription and a specific caveat: a fixed-view cache breaks their consistency condition, which is exactly the regime where they observed student overfitting to the teacher — hence the K=4 view bank. Caveat on the extrapolation: this is single-teacher CLASSIFICATION distillation, not multi-teacher dense feature matching.

key_papers.citation: Garrido, Balestriero, Najman, LeCun. RankMe: Assessing the downstream performance of pretrained self-supervised representations by their rank. ICML 2023.
key_papers.why_relevant: Supplies diagnostic D1 as a concrete measurable quantity rather than an adjective: RankMe = exp(-sum p_k log p_k) over the normalized singular value spectrum. PHI-S applies it to published ViTs, which is what lets me pre-set the collapse threshold from healthy-model data (kill below 0.30 of ambient dim; pass at >=0.60, the SAM-H value) instead of picking a number after seeing our student.

honest_limitations: Nothing was trained. Every quantitative expectation here — including the 0.33-0.42 GA r range for the codes — is an argued estimate from a design analysis, not a measurement.

The supervision-bits argument counts TARGETS, not information. The 956,416 final-layer scalars per image is exact; the discounts applied to it (x0.85 for PHI-S-observed ambient-rank slack, x1/16 for spatial redundancy between neighbouring patch tokens, leaving ~5x10^4 effectively independent targets per image) are plausible bounds, not measured mutual information. The qualitative conclusion — that dense feature regression is a categorically different learning problem from a single scalar GA label, and that the from-scratch ResNet-18 failure therefore does not transfer — is robust to those factors. The absolute bit counts are not.

The four encoders' activation statistics have NOT been compared. PHI-S's central result is that this determines whether balancing is possible at all, so if FetalCLIP/USF-MAE/USFM/DINOv2 differ the way their teachers did (global std 0.0049 to 5.4688), the balancing problem is materially harder than the recommendation assumes.

No literature precedent exists for multi-teacher distillation at 20k images with ULTRASOUND teachers. The small-data anchor (Beyer, Flowers102 at 1,020 and Pets at 3,312 images) is single-teacher classification distillation, not multi-teacher dense feature matching. That extrapolation is mine and is the weakest link in the feasibility argument.

Diversity, not image count, is the binding constraint, and it cannot be argued away: our 20,413 frames are 686x fewer distinct images than DUNE (the smallest agglomerative work) and 68,584x fewer than AM-RADIO, from one cohort, one GA window (26-39wk), a handful of planes, with effective independent n = 908 fetuses at ~22.5 frames each.

The 10 min/epoch live-teacher figure is the user's. The ~40 s/epoch cached figure is my estimate for a ViT-B on 20.4k images and must be measured before a schedule is committed; the whole affordability argument rests on it.

Caching teacher targets breaks Beyer's consistency condition (student and teacher seeing the same augmented view) — exactly the regime where they observed student overfitting to the teacher. The K=4 view bank mitigates but does not eliminate this, and whichever choice is made must be reported.

Config B remains superior on one axis that no diagnostic can fix: it is data-independent, so it cannot absorb cohort idiosyncrasy. If cross-cohort stability matters more to the paper than per-teacher decodability, config B wins outright and this arm should not be run at all.

The clinical set (30,257 frames, GA 6.2-41.6wk) is the natural stage-1 corpus and would substantially relieve the diversity constraint, but it is a different cohort with different acquisition and mixing it in CHANGES WHAT THE CODEBOOK DESCRIBES. That is a scientific decision for the user, not an implementation detail.

Expected accuracy gain over the fixed random projection is small and possibly negative: config B already retains 82% of the FetalCLIP ceiling (0.385 of 0.469), leaving 0.084 r of total headroom, and the paper explicitly does not need a better GA clock. The honest case for this arm is per-teacher decodability, not accuracy.

A reviewer-facing weakness with no technical answer: 'you trained a model on 20k images in order to interpret models trained on millions.' It can only be met with the D1-D10 diagnostics reported in full, not with a better r.
Distillation.cost_estimate: PRECONDITION (no training): per-teacher activation statistics + RankMe on 20,413 frames — under 1 day, mostly existing forward passes. CACHING: 39 GB fp16 for one view of final-layer targets across all four teachers (956,416 scalars/image); 156 GB for the K=4 view bank recommended to preserve Beyer consistency. Do NOT cache all 88 layers — 1,047 GB for one view, 4,186 GB at K=4. STAGE 1 TRAINING: the user's 10 min/epoch live 4-teacher forward makes the literature-equivalent schedules infeasible (DUNE examples-seen equivalent = 6,276 epochs over IMPACT = 1,050 GPU-hours = 44 days; RADIO equivalent = 30,079 epochs = 5,000 GPU-hours = 208 days). With teachers cached, student-only forward/backward on a ViT-B over 20.4k images is ~40 s/epoch (MY ESTIMATE — measure before committing), so 1,000 epochs = ~11 GPU-hours and 3,000 = ~33; even the 6,276-epoch DUNE-equivalent is ~70 GPU-hours. Per-fold student refit for the leakage-clean headline: 5 x 1,000 epochs = ~56 GPU-hours. PARAMETERS: ViT-B/16 backbone 85.8M + 11.0M in four final-layer heads (hidden 1536). If depth is preserved naively, 88 per-layer heads = 264.5M head parameters, more head than backbone — hence the 3-depth-group compromise at 12 heads. STAGE 2: the existing EMA VQ, unchanged, hours not days. TOTAL for the recommended protocol: ~100-150 GPU-hours on one node plus ~156 GB storage, i.e. under a week of wall-clock, dominated by the per-fold refits rather than by any single student.

Projection.recommendation: Do NOT regularise a learned projection whose output is also the reconstruction target — break the coupling by construction instead. Keep the four encoders frozen; put the LEARNED map only on the ENCODER side of the VQ bottleneck (per-encoder MLP d_e->256, then mean->shared EMA codebook, deviation->private codebook as now); and make the reconstruction target the FROZEN RAW z-scored patch features at full dimensionality (24,576/9,216/9,216/61,440), predicted by a learned per-encoder decoder head from concat(shared_code, private_code). Because the target has no parameters, its variance is a constant of the dataset and collapse becomes structurally impossible rather than merely penalised: any variance the learned map discards appears as unrecoverable reconstruction error. This also removes the need to tune an anti-collapse coefficient, which in our setting could only be tuned against GA — the outcome under study. Explicitly DROP the learned-orthonormal-projection option: orthonormality constrains geometry WITHIN the retained subspace but not WHICH subspace is retained, and 'discard the high-variance directions' is a perfectly orthonormal move. Run it as a pre-registered head-to-head against the seeded random projection at matched 256d and matched codebook, GroupKFold-by-fetus, bootstrap CI>=2000, with effective rank and codebook usage as primary collapse diagnostics; report a null as a null if the CI on the difference straddles zero.
Projection.mechanism: FROZEN: all four encoders (FetalCLIP ViT-L/14 24x1024, USF-MAE 12x768, USFM 12x768, DINOv2 ViT-g/14 40x1536); the layerwise z-scoring statistics; and critically the RECONSTRUCTION TARGET, which is the raw z-scored patch-feature tensor resampled to the common 14x14 grid and has zero parameters. LEARNED: (1) per-encoder encoder-side maps E_e: d_e -> 256 (non-linear MLP permitted, since no PCA-equivalence theorem applies and it is never the target); (2) per-encoder decoder heads D_e: 512 -> d_e, i.e. from concat(shared_code, private_code) back into that encoder's own native feature space; (3) the EMA codebooks (shared, on the arithmetic mean of the 256-d maps across encoders; private, on each encoder's deviation from that mean), with dead-code reinit retained — a gradient codebook previously collapsed to 9/32 codes on this project and EMA fixed it. LOSS: MSE (or cosine, fixed in advance) between D_e(codes) and the FROZEN RAW z_e, summed over encoders, plus the standard EMA-VQ commitment term. No variance floor, no whitening operator, no stop-gradient is required, because the degenerate optimum they exist to block does not exist once the target is parameter-free. Outcome labels (SGA, birth percentile, PE, NICU, GA) are evaluation-only and never enter any loss. Sizing: 18.9M trainable params for a 6-layer-per-encoder subset (80.2M all-layer); the decoder head D_e doubles as the interpretation device, since a shared code can be pushed through it and read as a pattern in FetalCLIP's own 24x1024 dims.
Projection.circularity_analysis: The interpretability claim remains valid, on four grounds. (1) No encoder is fine-tuned on any outcome — encoders stay frozen, so the project's hard constraint against studying GA structure in codes derived from GA-supervised features is respected. (2) The learned map is trained ONLY to reconstruct frozen features; GA/SGA/PE/NICU never appear in the objective, so no axis is defined via the outcome it is then tested against. (3) No hyperparameter is tuned against the outcome. This is the specific circularity that VICReg-style anti-collapse would have introduced: mu/nu are normally tuned against downstream accuracy, and our only downstream is GA, so tuning anti-collapse strength against GA r would make the subsequent GA analysis circular. The frozen-target design needs no such coefficient. (4) The user's PCA objection is not evaded by wording: the raw features are never replaced as the object of study — they remain the reconstruction target at full dimensionality, and the learned map is an analysis path INTO the codebook rather than a substitute basis. By contrast the learned orthonormal projection IS PCA-by-another-name and should be dropped: reconstruction-optimal linear maps recover the principal subspace (Bourlard & Kamp 1988; Baldi & Hornik 1989) up to invertible transformation, and an added orthogonality penalty recovers the principal directions themselves. Residual (non-circular but real) risks are ordinary leakage risks, handled by the diagnostics: fetus grouping in GroupKFold, no GA reintroduction, and a GA-label-shuffle refit that must drive r to chance.
Projection.kill_criterion: Dead if, on held-out fetuses under GroupKFold-by-fetus with bootstrap CI >= 2000 resamples, the learned encoder-side map FAILS to beat the seeded random projection on raw-feature reconstruction at matched 256-d width and matched codebook capacity — the CI on the difference straddling zero — WHILE its effective rank is no higher than the random projection's. That conjunction means the learned map bought neither fidelity nor richer geometry, and the 18.9M extra parameters and 25-50 GPU-hours are unjustified: keep the fixed random projection and report the null. Two auxiliary kills, each fatal on its own: (a) held-out-ENCODER reconstruction collapses when the shared codebook is fit on 3 encoders and only a head is fit for the 4th — the 'shared' code is then an artefact of joint fitting; (b) code-conditioned readouts through D_e are unstable across folds (the same shared code maps to unrelated patterns in different folds), which kills the interpretability rationale specifically even if reconstruction improves. Note also that a null here is a genuine result for an interpretability paper — 'the random projection was already sufficient' — and must not be escaped by sweeping further constructions.

failure_modes.mode: Information-selective collapse: the learned map keeps a full-rank but information-POOR subspace
failure_modes.why_it_happens: If the projection output is also the target, the optimiser lowers loss by making the target trivially predictable. Verified analytically on a synthetic anisotropic spectrum: over a family of orthonormal projections of fixed width, Spearman(loss, variance retained) = +1.00, the optimum sits on the LOWEST-variance subspace, and it achieves ~116x lower loss than the PCA subspace. Orthonormality does not prevent this because it does not constrain which subspace is chosen; batch-whitening methods have likewise been shown to impose only a full-rank constraint, and full rank is much weaker than informative.
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: Effective rank (RankMe: exp of the entropy of the normalised covariance eigenvalues) of the 256-d projected features on HELD-OUT fetuses, learned vs seeded-random, plus the fraction of each encoder's raw feature variance linearly recoverable from the 256-d map. Pass bar: erank_learned >= erank_random AND recoverable-variance_learned >= random (random retains only 1.04% for FetalCLIP, 0.42% for DINOv2 at k=256).
failure_modes.known_fix: Structural: make the target the frozen raw features, so the loss-information correlation flips to -1.00 (optimum on the HIGHEST-variance subspace). This is the construction used by SAE interpretability (targets are saved activations of a frozen base model) and by agglomerative multi-teacher distillation (frozen teachers, learned adaptor heads on the student side).

failure_modes.mode: Dimensional collapse / shrinking variance in the 256-d projected space
failure_modes.why_it_happens: Standard SSL collapse: dimensions drift to near-constant, which is degenerate even when total rank looks acceptable.
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: Per-dimension variance across held-out tokens, tracked per epoch: report min, 5th percentile, and the count of dims with variance < 0.01x the mean dim variance. Pass bar: zero dims below that floor and no downward drift across epochs. Track alongside effective rank, since RankMe has been reported to lose its correlation with downstream quality in some imbalanced/application-specific domains, so it should not be the sole monitor.
failure_modes.known_fix: VICReg-style hinge on per-dimension std plus covariance decorrelation would fix this directly and needs no stop-gradient or BN — but note it makes our objective DEGENERATE: with a per-dim unit-variance floor the reconstruction loss becomes numerically identical (0.7500) for the PCA and anti-PCA subspaces, so it must be a monitor here, not the primary defence.

failure_modes.mode: Codebook collapse / dead codes
failure_modes.why_it_happens: With argmin assignment and a straight-through estimator only the selected code receives gradient, so unselected codes drift into dead codes. This project already hit it: a gradient codebook collapsed to 9/32 codes. Low effective dimensionality of the input activations is itself correlated with higher dead-feature proportions.
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: Codes used per epoch out of 256 (shared and each private book separately) and code-histogram perplexity exp(-sum p log p), plus mean quantisation error. Pass bar: >=90% usage sustained (current design achieves 256/256). Usage and perplexity alone can be misleading — methods reaching 100% usage can still be badly misaligned with the latent distribution — so always report quantisation error beside them.
failure_modes.known_fix: Retain EMA codebook updates and dead-code reinit (already fixed this once here). If it recurs, the rotation trick restructures the VQ backward pass and has raised usage from 2% to 27% in a 16384-code VQGAN while cutting quantisation error by two orders of magnitude.

failure_modes.mode: Decoder memorisation: the learned head reconstructs without the code carrying content
failure_modes.why_it_happens: The decoder heads have real capacity (53.5M params all-layer) and could reproduce per-encoder mean structure from bias and dataset statistics alone, making recon look good while the discrete code is nearly ignored.
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: Code-ablation battery on held-out fetuses: (a) replace each token's code with a uniformly random code, (b) replace with the marginal-mode code, (c) reconstruct from the decoder bias alone with codes zeroed. Pass bar: large, reported degradation under (a) and (b), and near-zero explained variance under (c). If recon barely moves under ablation, the codebook is decorative.
failure_modes.known_fix: Cap decoder capacity (linear or single-hidden-layer head), and report the ablation deltas as a headline number rather than only the recon value.

failure_modes.mode: The 'shared' code is an artefact of jointly fitting all four encoders
failure_modes.why_it_happens: A map trained on all four simultaneously can encode encoder-specific nuisance (scanner/preprocessing signature) in the shared book and still reconstruct everything well.
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: Held-out-ENCODER test: fit the shared codebook on 3 encoders, freeze it, then fit ONLY a new decoder head for the 4th. Compare its reconstruction to the shared code trained with all four, and compare against the random-projection version of the same experiment. Pass bar: held-out-encoder recon within a pre-stated margin; if it collapses, 'shared' does not mean shared.
failure_modes.known_fix: Report the held-out-encoder number as a primary result, not a supplement. Multi-teacher distillation work treats exactly this per-teacher fidelity through the adaptor head as a defining quality criterion.

failure_modes.mode: Overfitting the small cohort / leakage through fetus grouping
failure_modes.why_it_happens: 20,413 frames from 908 fetuses is small: 18.9M params for the 6-layer subset is ~20,787 params per fetus, and patch tokens are not independent samples (~4,406 tokens per fetus). A from-scratch ResNet-18 already failed to learn ultrasound features from pixels on this data (MAE 0.90wk, near-identical Grad-CAMs).
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: GroupKFold-by-fetus with no fetus in both train and test; report the train-vs-held-out reconstruction gap per fold and its stability, and confirm effective sample size is counted in FETUSES not tokens. Also confirm no last-slot/aggregation bug by shuffling token order within a frame (recon must be invariant).
failure_modes.known_fix: Prefer the 6-layer-per-encoder subset (18.9M params, 183 GB cache) over all-layer (80.2M, 0.76 TB cache — infeasible), choose the layer subset BEFORE looking at any outcome, and keep the map deliberately small.

failure_modes.mode: Silent outcome leakage into the learned map
failure_modes.why_it_happens: Any accidental use of GA (as input, as a tuning signal, or via GA-correlated sampling/batching) would make the subsequent GA analysis circular.
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: Negative-control battery: (a) refit the entire pipeline on GA-label-SHUFFLED data — GA r decoded from codes must fall to chance; (b) PE as a maternal negative control; (c) confirm by code inspection that no outcome tensor is reachable from the loss.
failure_modes.known_fix: Outcomes remain evaluation-only by construction; no hyperparameter selected on any outcome; primary comparison fixed before any r/AUC is computed.

failure_modes.mode: Scanner/plane confound absorbed into the shared code
failure_modes.why_it_happens: A learned map has more freedom than a random one to align its 256 dims with acquisition nuisance. NMF topics over the code histogram were already a null on this project and their extra factors encoded imaging PLANE at eta^2 up to 0.78.
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: eta^2 of the code histogram on plane and on scanner/dataset, and GA r after regressing plane out (95% of GA r survived plane-residualisation with the random projection). Pass bar: plane eta^2 no worse than the random-projection baseline, and plane-residual GA r retained.
failure_modes.known_fix: Report plane/scanner eta^2 beside every recon and GA number; if the learned map worsens plane entanglement, that is a reason to keep the random projection even if recon improves.

key_papers.citation: Bardes, Ponce & LeCun. VICReg: Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization for Self-Supervised Learning. ICLR 2022.
key_papers.why_relevant: The explicit anti-collapse reference: a hinge keeping each embedding dimension's std above a threshold plus pairwise decorrelation, needing no stop-gradient, BN or quantisation. Adopted here as a MONITOR, not the primary defence — with a per-dim variance floor our reconstruction loss becomes numerically identical (0.7500) for the PCA and anti-PCA subspaces, so it cannot detect information-selective collapse, and its coefficients could only be tuned honestly against GA, which is circular.

key_papers.citation: Chen & He. Exploring Simple Siamese Representation Learning (SimSiam). CVPR 2021.
key_papers.why_relevant: Establishes that stop-gradient alone prevents collapse (removing it drops ImageNet linear probe from 67.7% to 0.1%; predictor/BN/L2-norm architecture does not save it). Assessed and REJECTED for transfer: the mechanism is a fixed-point argument between two branches of one trainable encoder, whereas our target is a deterministic function of the projection, so stop-grad removes the incentive to shrink the target without removing the ability to.

key_papers.citation: Grill et al. Bootstrap Your Own Latent (BYOL): a new approach to self-supervised learning. NeurIPS 2020.
key_papers.why_relevant: The momentum-encoder target, i.e. an EMA target network that enforces an implicit stop-gradient. The closest existing analogue to 'a slowly-moving learned target', and the reason we prefer a strictly frozen target: an EMA target still drifts, so its variance is not a constant of the dataset.

key_papers.citation: Ermolov, Siarohin, Sangineto & Sebe. Whitening for Self-Supervised Representation Learning (W-MSE). ICML 2021.
key_papers.why_relevant: The whitening/decorrelation route, whose scattering effect substitutes for negatives. Relevant as the strongest theoretical anti-collapse guarantee, but costly (per-batch covariance inverse, high variance, batch-slicing needed) and insufficient here per the Weng-style analysis that batch-whitening imposes only a full-rank constraint.

key_papers.citation: Huang et al. An Investigation into Whitening Loss for Self-supervised Learning. NeurIPS 2022.
key_papers.why_relevant: Directly undercuts the whitening/orthogonality defence for our purpose: shows hard-whitening methods such as W-MSE impose only FULL-RANK constraints on the embedding rather than true whitening. A full-rank projection onto the bottom-256 eigendirections is exactly our failure mode, so full rank is not evidence of an informative projection.

key_papers.citation: Garrido, Balestriero, Najman & LeCun. RankMe: Assessing the Downstream Performance of Pretrained Self-Supervised Representations by Their Rank. ICML 2023.
key_papers.why_relevant: Supplies the primary collapse diagnostic: a label-free effective-rank measure (exponential of the entropy of normalised covariance eigenvalues, after Roy & Vetterli 2007) that is cheap enough to monitor every epoch. Used as the learned-vs-random gate. Its reported failure to correlate with downstream quality in some imbalanced application domains is why we pair it with a per-dimension variance floor.

key_papers.citation: Ranzinger et al. AM-RADIO: Agglomerative Vision Foundation Model — Reduce All Domains Into One. CVPR 2024.
key_papers.why_relevant: The direct precedent for the recommended architecture: multiple heterogeneous frozen teachers (CLIP, DINOv2, SAM) distilled with small 2-layer MLP adaptor heads that map STUDENT features into each teacher's space, learning on the student side and never on the target side. Validates both the frozen-target choice and the decoder head D_e as a readout into each encoder's native feature space.

key_papers.citation: Cunningham, Ewart, Riggs, Huben & Sharkey. Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models.
key_papers.why_relevant: The interpretability-field precedent that the target must be frozen raw activations of a frozen base model, and that learned dictionaries are compared against PCA/ICA/random-direction baselines for interpretability — exactly the learned-vs-random comparison we pre-register, and support for keeping the random projection as the matched-capacity comparator.

key_papers.citation: Plaut. From Principal Subspaces to Principal Components with Linear Autoencoders.
key_papers.why_relevant: Settles the user's PCA objection honestly. Reconstruction-trained linear autoencoders span the principal subspace (Bourlard & Kamp 1988; Baldi & Hornik 1989) with the basis defined only up to invertible transformation, and the loading vectors are recoverable by SVD of the weight matrix. Therefore a learned orthonormal projection trained to reconstruct IS PCA-by-another-name and falls foul of the same objection — grounds for dropping that option.

key_papers.citation: Fifty et al. Restructuring Vector Quantization with the Rotation Trick. ICLR 2025.
key_papers.why_relevant: The fallback if codebook collapse recurs (this project already saw 9/32 codes with a gradient codebook). Replaces the straight-through gradient with a rotation/rescaling that preserves relative angle and magnitude, raising codebook usage from 2% to 27% in a 16384-code VQGAN and cutting quantisation error by two orders of magnitude. Also documents the limitation at near-zero encoder-output norms.

key_papers.citation: Roy & Vetterli. The Effective Rank: A Measure of Effective Dimensionality. EUSIPCO 2007.
key_papers.why_relevant: The underlying definition behind the effective-rank diagnostic — exponential of the entropy of the normalised eigenvalues, scale-invariant and real-valued with maximum equal to the representation dimension — which is what makes 'is the learned map keeping more directions than the random one?' a well-posed measurable question.

honest_limitations: The +1.00/-1.00 loss-vs-information contrast that drives this recommendation was verified analytically on a synthetic anisotropic feature spectrum with a fixed decoder-capacity assumption, NOT on measured IMPACT-cohort features. It establishes the sign of the incentive, not its magnitude in our data.

The claimed interpretability gain — reading a shared code through D_e back into FetalCLIP's own 24x1024 dims — is a structural argument, not a measured result. It needs its own cross-fold stability validation before any 'sharper interpretation' claim is made in the paper.

The most likely outcome is a NULL: the learned map may not beat the seeded random projection at matched capacity. This project's registry already contains settled nulls of this shape (NMF topics never beat the histogram they compress).

Nothing here fixes the two structural findings that limit the whole design: depth-specific content dominates the shared code (FULL recon 0.298 vs SHARED-ONLY 0.830), and GA is distributed across codes rather than compact (20 best codes r=0.271 vs all-320 r=0.385). Those are properties of the frozen features, not of the projection.

Multiplicity is real: learned-vs-random x {all-layer, 6-layer} x {MSE, cosine} x {shared-only, full recon} is 16 constructions. Exactly one primary comparison must be fixed before any r/AUC is seen, with the rest labelled exploratory and the bar adjusted.

The 6-layer-per-encoder subset is a pragmatic concession to the 0.76 TB all-layer cache, and it discards depth information that the established depth-factorisation result says matters. The subset must be chosen before seeing outcomes.

A frozen raw target does not make the learned map immune to fitting acquisition nuisance (scanner, plane) rather than anatomy; it only removes the target-shrinking degeneracy. Plane eta^2 must be reported beside every reconstruction number.

Effective rank is an imperfect gate — it has been reported not to correlate with downstream quality in some imbalanced, application-specific domains, which is why it is paired with a per-dimension variance floor and code-ablation rather than trusted alone.
Cost is non-trivial against a single GPU node (25-50 GPU-hours for a properly cross-validated comparison), so this should not be run before the primary comparison and kill criterion are written down.
Design-and-literature only: nothing was trained, no cohort data was read, and no existing config-B model or repository state was modified.
Projection.cost_estimate: Live 4-encoder forward pass at ~10 min/epoch on the one GPU node: 30 epochs x 5 GroupKFold folds = 25 GPU-hours; 60 epochs x 5 folds = 50 GPU-hours (~2 days). Precomputing features to avoid the live pass is infeasible at all layers (4.0M patch tokens x 104,448 dims = 0.76 TB fp16) but practical for a 6-evenly-spaced-layers-per-encoder subset (24,576 dims, 183 GB fp16), which is the recommended route and cuts per-epoch cost substantially. Trainable parameters: 18.9M (6-layer subset) or 80.2M (all-layer: 26.7M encoder-side maps + 53.5M decoder heads). Frozen raw targets held on device are cheap — 1.22 GB fp16 at batch 32 all-layer, 0.29 GB for the 6-layer subset — so the frozen-target design adds negligible memory over the current one. Diagnostics (effective rank, per-dim variance, codebook usage/perplexity, code ablation) are SVD-and-histogram cheap and can run every epoch; the held-out-encoder test costs one extra head-only fit per encoder.

Interpretability.recommendation: Add nothing learned between the frozen encoders and the codebook: keep the fixed random projection and adopt the proposed raw-unprojected-feature code characterisation, which is exact and sound. But do NOT proceed to characterise the shared vocabulary until question 0 has been answered, because the current shared/private construction has an arithmetic null floor nobody has subtracted. Defining shared = arithmetic mean over E encoders means the mean carries exactly 1/E of the variance when the true shared fraction is ZERO -- 25% at E=4 -- so an observed 'shared explains ~25-30%' is inside the null (0.30 apparent implies only 0.067 true sharing), and the private deviations are rank E-1=3, not 4, so one private codebook is redundant with the others. Run, in this order, on the features that already exist and with no training: (1) the analytic 1/E floor plus an encoder-shuffle empirical floor (each patch's four feature vectors drawn from four different patches, destroying correspondence while preserving marginals); (2) per-encoder codebooks fitted separately and compared for cross-vocabulary agreement under >=3 measures (code-assignment AMI/ARI, Mantel on RDMs, Procrustes/shape distance), permuting WHOLE FETUSES and computing within imaging plane; (3) per code per encoder the mean of the raw unprojected features PLUS within/between-code dispersion and a held-out faithfulness leg (does mu_e(k) beat the global mean and a matched-granularity random partition at predicting that encoder's held-out patch features). Keep d=256 and add d=1024 as a robustness column, not a redesign. Reject the learned projection outright -- it is the one option where the reconstruction target is itself optimised. Consider a distilled student ONLY if step (1) shows genuine sharing above the floor, and then only as a secondary analysis reported alongside the random-projection result. Take seriously that the honest outcome may be a NULL: given that the depth-shared component already reconstructs almost nothing (0.830 vs 0.298 full) among layers that share weights, data and objective, four independently-trained encoders should share less, and 'there is no common visual vocabulary across fetal-ultrasound foundation models beyond a low-level plane/framing axis' is a publishable, well-powered negative result and a direct domain-specific rebuttal to the Platonic Representation Hypothesis.
Interpretability.mechanism: RECOMMENDED (nothing learned). FROZEN: all four encoders (FetalCLIP ViT-L/14, USF-MAE ViT-B/16, USFM ViT-B/16, DINOv2 ViT-g/14), patch tokens, all layers. FIXED, DATA-INDEPENDENT: per-encoder layerwise z-score -> seeded Gaussian random projection of the all-layer concatenation to a common 256-d -> resample grids to 14x14. LEARNED: only the EMA codebook with dead-code reinit (the quantiser itself), fitted with the standard VQ objective (assignment + commitment) on the projected features. LOSS: reconstruction of the projected features only. Outcome labels (GA, SGA, birth percentile, PE, NICU) never enter any loss or any feature-construction step -- they are evaluation-only. CODE CHARACTERISATION (the new part, and it fits NOTHING): the codebook only partitions patches; for each code k and each encoder e report mu_e(k) = mean of the RAW UNPROJECTED patch features of patches assigned to k, computed in that encoder's own native space. This is a conditional mean over an index set -- exact, no pseudo-inverse, no decoder, no inversion of a rank-deficient map -- so it cannot collapse because nothing is optimised. Reported alongside: within-code/between-code native variance ratio, fraction of within-code variance on the code's top native PC, held-out predictive gain of mu_e(k) over the global mean and over a matched-granularity random partition, and exemplar patch montages. CONDITIONAL FALLBACK (only if the null battery shows real sharing): distilled student trained to match the four FROZEN teachers' patch features via cosine loss through per-teacher 2-layer MLP adaptor heads (AM-RADIO), with per-teacher distribution balancing (PHI-S) because teacher activation scales differ by orders of magnitude and an unbalanced MSE silently reweights teachers. Teachers stay frozen so the target cannot move; outcomes still never enter the loss; every codebook result is reported BOTH student-based and random-projection-based.
Interpretability.circularity_analysis: The interpretability claim survives under the recommended design, and the line is not 'learned vs fixed' -- random projection is data-independent, which is a weaker virtue than unbiased. Three properties get conflated and must be separated. (i) DATA-INDEPENDENCE: the map is fixed before seeing this cohort -- true for random projection, false for both learned options. (ii) OUTCOME-INDEPENDENCE: the fitted object never sees GA/SGA/PE -- true for all three, provided the loss is reconstruction/teacher-matching only. (iii) TARGET-INDEPENDENCE: the reconstruction target is not itself being optimised -- true for random projection and for a distilled student (teachers frozen), FALSE for a learned projection, which can shrink or collapse its own target to lower the loss. The user's stated worry is precisely this target-independence failure, it is real, and it is specific to the learned projection; it is NOT circularity in the outcome sense. A distilled student does not have it. So the genuine line is: legitimate representation learning fits an object with a loss that never references the evaluation outcome AND scopes the claim to what was actually fitted; the finding becomes 'about my own fitted model' when a property of the fitted object is reported as a property of the encoders without a faithfulness measurement licensing that transfer. That second failure happens by omission, not intent. With a fixed projection, a code is (approximately) a region of the frozen feature space and nothing was fitted to make it so, so 'here is what fetal-ultrasound foundation models encode' is supportable. With a distilled student the defensible title narrows to 'a discrete vocabulary learned by agreement across four encoders' -- a claim about the consensus object, not about any encoder. That is still publishable; the danger is that the swap is easy to make silently. Two further circularity traps specific to this project: (a) a shared axis must not be defined via the outcome it is then tested against -- if a code subset is selected for GA-relatedness and then evaluated on GA, the result is circular by construction, and this project has already measured that GA is DISTRIBUTED (20 best codes r=0.271 vs all-320 0.385), so selection would be both circular and weak; (b) the literature's hardest warning for any dictionary method is that SAEs trained on RANDOMLY INITIALISED transformers score similarly on auto-interpretability and reconstruction to those trained on real ones, so 'the codes look coherent and readable' is NOT evidence the encoders learned anything -- the dictionary's inductive bias plus the data distribution suffice. Every code-quality claim therefore needs a matched control, not a qualitative reading.
Interpretability.kill_criterion: THE SHARED-VOCABULARY FRAMING IS DEAD IF, on the four-encoder projected features that already exist: the shared/private variance split sits inside the encoder-shuffle floor band -- equivalently observed apparent-shared <= ~0.30 at E=4, implying true shared fraction <= ~0.07 against the exact 1/E=0.25 floor -- AND cross-vocabulary agreement between separately-fitted per-encoder codebooks fails to exceed its WHOLE-FETUS permutation null once computed within imaging plane, under >=2 of 3 similarity measures. In that case there is no common vocabulary to describe, the shared/private codebook should be dropped rather than reported, and the paper's contribution becomes the negative result: no common visual vocabulary exists across fetal-ultrasound foundation models beyond a low-level plane/framing axis -- a domain-specific rebuttal to the Platonic Representation Hypothesis. THE RAW-FEATURE CHARACTERISATION IS DEAD IF within-code native variance is indistinguishable from global variance (ratio -> 1) for most codes in most encoders, and mu_e(k) fails to beat a matched-granularity random partition at predicting held-out patch features: the codes would be arbitrary bins and the means would describe nothing. THE DISTILLED STUDENT IS DEAD IF per-teacher held-out faithfulness is low for any teacher while codebook results look BETTER than the random-projection substrate (the signature of invented structure), or if student-based and projection-based conclusions disagree at all.

failure_modes.mode: 1/E null floor: the arithmetic mean looks 'shared' when nothing is shared
failure_modes.why_it_happens: With shared := mean over E encoders and private := deviation, under a null of zero true sharing var(mean)=s_u2/E and var(dev)=s_u2(1-1/E), so the mean carries exactly 1/E of the variance -- 25% at E=4 -- purely arithmetically. Observed 'shared explains 25-30%' is inside the null; 0.30 apparent implies only 0.067 true sharing.
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: Compare the observed shared/private variance split against (a) the analytic 1/E floor and (b) an empirical floor from re-running the full pipeline on encoder-shuffled features (each patch's four vectors taken from four different patches, destroying cross-encoder correspondence while preserving every marginal). Report the observed split as a z-score or percentile against that shuffle band, never as a bare percentage.
failure_modes.known_fix: Report shared strength only as excess over the shuffle floor. If it does not clear the band, drop the shared/private framing and report the null.

failure_modes.mode: Rank deficiency of the private streams
failure_modes.why_it_happens: Deviations from the mean sum to zero by construction, so for E=4 the four private streams span only rank 3 per feature. One private codebook is partly redundant with the other three, and a 'private' code is implicitly a statement about the other encoders.
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: Compute the numerical rank of the E-by-E deviation operator (expect E-1=3) and the rank/effective dimension of the stacked private features. Check whether any one encoder's private codes are predictable from the other three's.
failure_modes.known_fix: Use E-1 private codebooks with an explicit reference encoder, or predict each encoder's features from a leave-one-encoder-out mean (a crossed/cross-view construction) so no encoder contributes to the target it is reconstructed from.

failure_modes.mode: Mimic effect: cross-encoder agreement manufactured by a shared confound (imaging plane)
failure_modes.why_it_happens: RSA/Mantel is a second-order statistic, so systems operating on entirely different features can have highly correlated representational geometries when the stimulus set carries a confound both systems respond to. Plane is the dominant nuisance here (NMF extra factors reached eta2=0.78 on plane). Simulated at this project's scale with two encoders whose mechanisms are independent BY CONSTRUCTION and share only the plane label, Mantel r reached 0.695 (within-plane: 0.017).
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: Recompute every cross-encoder agreement statistic WITHIN a single imaging plane and after adjusting for plane/GA/scanner/dataset/image-count; also compute agreement between one real encoder and a random-weight encoder of matched architecture. If pooled agreement is high but within-plane agreement collapses to the permutation band, the agreement was the confound.
failure_modes.known_fix: Report within-plane (confound-conditioned) agreement as the primary number; treat pooled agreement as the upper bound including confound. Deconfound via covariate-adjustment regression on the similarity matrices.

failure_modes.mode: Pseudo-replication: permuting patches instead of fetuses
failure_modes.why_it_happens: Mantel/permutation assumes exchangeable units, but 4.0M patch tokens come from only 908 fetuses (~4,400 patches/fetus). Design effect 1+(m-1)*ICC gives effective n of 88,805 at ICC=0.01, 9,061 at 0.10 and 1,816 at 0.50; at ICC=0.10 the standard error is optimistic by ~21x. Documented Mantel failure: autocorrelation in BOTH matrices inflates the statistic and type I error, and the PARTIAL Mantel test does not fix it.
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: Estimate the within-fetus ICC of the patch features (currently unmeasured in this project) and report the implied effective n. Build the null by permuting whole fetuses and verify the patch-level null is visibly narrower than the fetus-level null.
failure_modes.known_fix: Permute at the fetus level only (GroupKFold-by-fetus already in the protocol must extend to the permutation scheme); report effective rather than nominal n.

failure_modes.mode: Similarity-measure fragility: the conclusion depends on which metric was chosen
failure_modes.why_it_happens: CKA is formally sensitive to a broad class of simple transformations and can be manipulated to arbitrarily high or low values while functional behaviour is preserved; RSA and CKA are both confounded by input population structure, which can make completely random networks look spuriously similar; the measures demonstrably disagree on basic questions such as whether differently-seeded networks learn similar representations.
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: Report agreement under >=3 measures (code-assignment AMI/ARI, Mantel on RDMs, Procrustes/shape distance which satisfies the triangle inequality) and require the qualitative conclusion to be invariant. Ground functionally where possible: sensitivity to changes that alter behaviour, specificity against changes that do not.
failure_modes.known_fix: Pre-specify the measure set and the invariance requirement before looking at results; prefer model stitching for functional grounding, since it reveals aspects CKA cannot.

failure_modes.mode: Codes are bins on a continuum, not natural kinds
failure_modes.why_it_happens: This project has measured silhouette <=0.30 everywhere -- the latent is a continuum. Quantising it yields bins whose identities are not stable objects. Measured code-assignment reproducibility on a continuum-like anisotropic substrate is only ARI ~0.30 across projection seeds, versus ~0.70 on a genuinely clustered substrate through the same projection.
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: Seed-stability decomposition: ARI across projection seeds versus ARI across k-means inits at a FIXED projection. Measured gap is only +0.079 (d=256) and +0.053 (d=1024), i.e. most instability is intrinsic to the continuum, not the projection. Also report per-code within/between native-variance ratio.
failure_modes.known_fix: Make all claims aggregate and distributional ('this region of the space behaves thus'), never 'code 137 means X'. State plainly in the paper that codes are bins on a gradient. d=1024 buys ~+0.05 ARI at 4x cost -- a robustness column, not a redesign.

failure_modes.mode: Interpretability illusion: readable codes that are not a property of the encoder
failure_modes.why_it_happens: SAEs trained on randomly initialised transformers yield auto-interpretability and reconstruction scores broadly similar to trained ones, so dictionary readability reflects the dictionary's inductive bias plus the data distribution. Separately, maximally-activating-example patterns are consistent within a dataset but not across datasets, and simplified proxies faithful in-distribution become less faithful out of distribution.
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: Fit the identical codebook pipeline on a RANDOM-WEIGHT encoder of matched architecture and on shuffled features; compare code coherence, usage entropy and exemplar-montage readability. If the random-weight control looks comparably interpretable, code readability is not evidence about the encoders. Also test code stability across a held-out cohort split (clinical vs IMPACT).
failure_modes.known_fix: Report every code-quality metric as excess over the random-weight control; validate codes on a held-out dataset rather than the fitting set.

failure_modes.mode: Learned projection collapses or shrinks its own reconstruction target
failure_modes.why_it_happens: When the learned projection is simultaneously the reconstruction TARGET, the loss can be reduced by shrinking, low-ranking or collapsing the target rather than by learning structure -- a degenerate optimum with no informative content. This is exactly the target-independence failure.
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: Track target scale and effective rank (participation ratio / singular-value spectrum) of the projected space across training; monitor codebook usage and perplexity; compare reconstruction loss against the loss of a random projection of matched output dimension. A falling loss with falling target variance or falling effective rank is collapse.
failure_modes.known_fix: Do not use a learned projection. If a learned intermediate is wanted, use a distilled student against FROZEN teachers so the target cannot move -- with PHI-S per-teacher distribution balancing, since teacher activation scales differ by orders of magnitude.

failure_modes.mode: Distilled student invents structure the teachers do not have
failure_modes.why_it_happens: A student optimised to match four teachers can satisfy the aggregate objective while being unfaithful to any individual teacher, especially when an unbalanced loss implicitly reweights teachers by activation scale. Codebook structure then reflects the student's own inductive bias.
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: Per-teacher held-out faithfulness (feature cosine/CKA per teacher, per layer) reported BEFORE any codebook result; and run the whole codebook analysis both student-based and random-projection-based. Low faithfulness for some teacher combined with BETTER-looking codebook results is the signature of invented structure; divergence between the two substrates is a finding about the student.
failure_modes.known_fix: PHI-S / Hadamard isotropic standardisation of teacher distributions; per-teacher adaptor heads; report both substrates and scope the claim to the consensus object rather than to any encoder.

failure_modes.mode: Multiplicity across constructions, endpoints and windows
failure_modes.why_it_happens: Many feature/pooling/codebook/endpoint combinations are available (E encoders x layer sets x d x K x endpoints x adjustment ladders); the best of many looks significant at an uncorrected bar. This project has already recorded artifacts of exactly this kind (a PC8 'ADD' that was 5 outlier fetuses).
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: Maintain an explicit count of constructions x endpoints x windows actually run and apply a correspondingly raised bar (Bonferroni/BH across the full family); report the whole family, not the survivor. Cross-check any survivor against the PE maternal negative control and a label-shuffle permutation.
failure_modes.known_fix: Freeze feature construction and the endpoint list before seeing outcome AUCs (already project protocol); pre-register the null battery of Rank 1 and report all arms.

failure_modes.mode: Conditional mean mu_e(k) describes a point where no data lives
failure_modes.why_it_happens: A code is a Voronoi cell in the PROJECTED 256-d space; its preimage in the native 1024-d space can be elongated or multi-modal, and the mean of a multi-modal set is not representative. Worst-case JL at d=256 over 4.0M patches is vacuous (eps=0.69; eps=0.10 would need d~12,000), even though typical single-pair distortion is only 8.8% and k-means-specific sketching guarantees hold at O(k/eps^2).
failure_modes.detecting_diagnostic: Per code per encoder: within-code/between-code native variance ratio, fraction of within-code variance on the code's top native PC, and multimodality tests on the native-space preimage. A ratio approaching 1 means the code is an arbitrary bin, not a concept.
failure_modes.known_fix: Always publish dispersion beside every mean; add the held-out faithfulness test (mu_e(k) vs global mean vs matched-granularity random partition); never make claims about individual patch pairs at d=256.

key_papers.citation: Heap, T., Lawson, T., Farnik, L., & Aitchison, L. (2025). Sparse Autoencoders Can Interpret Randomly Initialized Transformers.
key_papers.why_relevant: The single most damaging paper for a VQ/dictionary interpretability claim: SAEs on randomly initialised transformers produce auto-interpretability and reconstruction scores broadly similar to trained models. Implies 'our codes look coherent' is not evidence the encoders learned anything, and mandates a random-weight-encoder control for every code-quality metric.

key_papers.citation: Dujmovic, M., Bowers, J. S., Adolfi, F., & Malhotra, G. (2022). Some pitfalls of measuring representational similarity using Representational Similarity Analysis. bioRxiv.
key_papers.why_relevant: Documents the 'mimic' effect (stimulus confounds give high RSA between provably dissimilar systems) and the 'modulation' effect (scores depend on the test stimuli). Because RSA is second-order, systems using entirely different features can share representational geometry -- exactly the risk for the projection-free per-encoder-codebook comparison, where imaging plane is a strong shared confound (eta2 up to 0.78 in this cohort).

key_papers.citation: Davari, M., Horoi, S., Natik, A., Lajoie, G., Wolf, G., & Belilovsky, E. (2023). Reliability of CKA as a Similarity Measure in Deep Learning. ICLR.
key_papers.why_relevant: The requested documented criticism of CKA: formal characterisation of its sensitivity to simple affine transformations, explaining outlier sensitivity, and demonstrations that CKA can be driven arbitrarily high or low while functional behaviour is preserved. Reason to never rest a cross-encoder agreement conclusion on a single similarity measure.

key_papers.citation: Ding, F., Denain, J.-S., & Steinhardt, J. (2021). Grounding Representation Similarity with Statistical Testing. NeurIPS 34.
key_papers.why_relevant: Shows CCA/CKA/Procrustes disagree on fundamental questions and supplies the correct standard for choosing among them: sensitivity to changes that affect functional behaviour, specificity against changes that do not. This is the framework for pre-specifying the >=3-measure invariance requirement.

key_papers.citation: Cui, T., Kumar, Y., Marttinen, P., & Kaski, S. (2022). Deconfounded Representation Similarity for Comparison of Neural Networks. NeurIPS 35.
key_papers.why_relevant: Shows RSA and CKA are confounded by the population structure of the input data, which can make completely random networks look spuriously similar, and provides a covariate-adjustment-regression fix that retains the measures' invariances. Directly applicable to adjusting cross-encoder agreement for plane/GA/scanner.

key_papers.citation: Crabot, J., Clappe, S., Dray, S., & Datry, T. (2019). Testing the Mantel statistic with a spatially-constrained permutation procedure. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 10, 532-540.
key_papers.why_relevant: Establishes that when BOTH distance matrices are autocorrelated the Mantel statistic and its type I error are inflated, and that the PARTIAL Mantel test does not correct it. This is the pseudo-replication hazard for 4.0M patches from 908 fetuses, and the reason permutation must be at the fetus level.

key_papers.citation: Friedman, D., Lampinen, A., Dixon, L., Chen, D., & Ghandeharioun, A. (2024). Interpretability Illusions in the Generalization of Simplified Models. ICML.
key_papers.why_relevant: Simplified proxies (SVD, clustering -- the same family as a VQ codebook) can approximate a model faithfully in-distribution yet be less faithful out of distribution. Grounds the requirement that any code-level story be validated on a held-out cohort split rather than the fitting set.

key_papers.citation: Bolukbasi, T., Pearce, A., Yuan, A., Coenen, A., Reif, E., Viegas, F., & Wattenberg, M. (2021). An Interpretability Illusion for BERT.
key_papers.why_relevant: Coins the interpretability illusion: maximally-activating examples give consistent readable patterns per unit that are NOT consistent across datasets. Directly cautions against reading per-code exemplar montages as code semantics without cross-dataset replication.

key_papers.citation: Huh, M., Cheung, B., Wang, T., & Isola, P. (2024). Position: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis. ICML.
key_papers.why_relevant: The hypothesis that models trained differently converge to a shared statistical model of reality -- the theoretical claim the shared codebook implicitly assumes. If cross-encoder shared is near-empty here, the null is a substantive domain-specific rebuttal rather than a failed experiment, which is what makes the negative result publishable.

key_papers.citation: Back into Plato's Cave: Examining Cross-modal Representational Convergence at Scale (2026).
