key_papers.why_relevant: Empirical counterweight to the Platonic hypothesis: mutual-kNN agreement drops sharply from small galleries to million-scale, degrades further under many-to-many correspondence, and the 'stronger models align better' trend does not consistently hold. Supports the interpretation that alignment is local and partial -- precedent for reporting a fetal-ultrasound convergence null.

key_papers.citation: Thasarathan, H., Forsyth, J., Fel, T., Kowal, M., & Derpanis, K. G. (2025). Universal Sparse Autoencoders: Interpretable Cross-Model Concept Alignment. ICML (PMLR 267).
key_papers.why_relevant: The closest published relative of the shared-codebook design: one overcomplete SAE ingesting any model's activations and decoding to any other's, learning a universal concept space and reporting that concept universality correlates with importance. Essential related work -- but it does not address the 1/E floor, and Heap et al. is why its readable concepts are not self-validating.

key_papers.citation: Ranzinger, M., Heinrich, G., Kautz, J., & Molchanov, P. (2024). AM-RADIO: Agglomerative Vision Foundation Model -- Reduce All Domains Into One. CVPR.
key_papers.why_relevant: The reference recipe for the conditional fallback: multi-teacher distillation of heterogeneous frozen VFMs (CLIP/DINOv2/SAM) into one student via per-teacher 2-layer MLP adaptor heads with cosine feature-matching loss. Teachers stay frozen, so this is the option that avoids the learned projection's target-independence failure.

key_papers.citation: Ranzinger, M., Barker, J., Heinrich, G., Molchanov, P., Kautz, J., Catanzaro, B., & Tao, A. (2024). PHI-S: Distribution Balancing for Label-Free Multi-Teacher Distillation.
key_papers.why_relevant: Documents that teacher activation statistics differ enormously (SAM's std is ~191x DFN CLIP's), so MSE/Smooth-L1 silently weights teachers by scale, and gives Hadamard-based isotropic standardisation (PHI-S) as the fix. Mandatory if a student is ever built over these four very differently-scaled encoders.

key_papers.citation: Martens, K., & Yau, C. (2024). Disentangling shared and private latent factors in multimodal Variational Autoencoders. PMLR 240.
key_papers.why_relevant: Shows shared/private factorisations fail exactly in the regime this project is in -- modality-specific (here encoder-specific) variation dominating the shared signal -- because reconstructing many private features raises the objective more than reconstructing few shared ones. Supplies the stop-gradient remedy restricting shared-latent updates to cross-modal information.

key_papers.citation: Unsupervised discovery of the shared and private geometry in multi-view data (2024).
key_papers.why_relevant: Gives the crossed-autoencoder construction -- the shared latent used to reconstruct one view is always computed from the OTHER view, so private information provably cannot leak into shared -- plus a remedy for the reverse leak. This is the concrete fix for the rank-deficiency/self-inclusion defect in the mean-based shared/private split.

key_papers.citation: Moschella, L., Maiorca, V., Fumero, M., Norelli, A., Locatello, F., & Rodola, E. (2023). Relative representations enable zero-shot latent space communication. ICLR.
key_papers.why_relevant: Representing each sample by its similarities to a fixed anchor set yields invariance to latent isometries and rescalings with NO training and no shared projection -- a cheap, artifact-free alternative substrate for the cross-vocabulary comparison, and an alternative to random projection that keeps the design fully data-independent.

key_papers.citation: Bansal, Y., Nakkiran, P., & Barak, B. (2021). Revisiting Model Stitching to Compare Neural Representations. NeurIPS 34.
key_papers.why_relevant: Stitching frozen models A and B with one trainable layer reveals representational aspects CKA cannot, giving a functional rather than geometric notion of agreement. The right tool if a functionally-grounded cross-encoder comparison is wanted beyond RSA/CKA.

key_papers.citation: Williams, A. H., Kunz, E., Kornblith, S., & Linderman, S. W. (2021). Generalized Shape Metrics on Neural Representations. NeurIPS 34.
key_papers.why_relevant: Provides representational dissimilarity measures that are proper metrics (satisfying the triangle inequality), fixing a defect of raw CKA/CCA scores. Supplies the third, better-behaved measure for the >=3-measure invariance requirement.

key_papers.citation: Cohen, M. B., Elder, S., Musco, C., Musco, C., & Persu, M. (2015). Dimensionality Reduction for k-Means Clustering and Low Rank Approximation. STOC.
key_papers.why_relevant: Quantitative defence of the fixed random projection for THIS use: random projection to O(k/eps^2) dimensions is a (1+eps) projection-cost-preserving sketch for k-means, and O(log k/eps^2) suffices for a (9+eps) approximation -- so d=256 with K~256-320 is defensible for clustering cost even though all-pairs JL at 4.0M patches is vacuous (eps=0.69).

key_papers.citation: Fifty, C., Duan, R., Junkins, R. G., Amid, E., Leskovec, J., Re, C., & Thrun, S. (2024). Restructuring Vector Quantization with the Rotation Trick.
key_papers.why_relevant: Directly relevant to the collapse already experienced here (a gradient codebook fell to 9/32 codes before EMA fixed it): documents that the straight-through estimator discards quantiser information and causes collapse/under-utilisation, and gives a rotation-rescaling gradient that raised codebook usage substantially across 11 VQ paradigms. The fallback if EMA + dead-code reinit ever proves insufficient.

key_papers.citation: Hewitt, J., & Liang, P. (2019). Designing and Interpreting Probes with Control Tasks. EMNLP-IJCNLP, 2733-2743.
key_papers.why_relevant: The selectivity principle -- a probe's task accuracy is only interpretable against its accuracy on a random-label control of the same architecture -- is the template for the matched-capacity baselines and random-partition controls required when reporting what a code predicts.

key_papers.citation: Havasi, M., Parbhoo, S., & Doshi-Velez, F. (2022). Addressing Leakage in Concept Bottleneck Models. NeurIPS 35.
key_papers.why_relevant: The canonical account of concept leakage: when unintended information hides in soft concept scores, the bottleneck stops being interpretable and a supervisor can never tell whether a concept fires because it is present or because it encodes something else. The precise analogue of the risk that shared/private codes silently encode plane or scanner rather than fetal anatomy.

honest_limitations: The 1/E floor is exact and analytic, but the mimic-effect and seed-stability numbers are SIMULATIONS at this project's parameters, not measurements on the real features -- they demonstrate the failure modes are reachable at this scale, they do not estimate their actual magnitude here. Rank 1 replaces them with measurements.

The within-fetus ICC of patch features is NOT measured in this project, so the effective-n table (88,805 at ICC=0.01 down to 1,816 at 0.50) spans plausible values rather than reporting the truth; the real effective n is unknown until estimated.

The prediction that cross-encoder shared is emptier than depth-shared is an argument from coupling strength (layers share weights/data/objective; encoders do not) plus this project's encoder-ordered GA results (ResNet 0.19 < USFM 0.37 < FetalCLIP 0.47). It is falsifiable and could be wrong -- the four encoders might agree strongly on a low-level texture axis that happens to be substantive.

The seed-stability substrate was a synthetic heavy-tailed anisotropic Gaussian (participation ratio 88 of 3072) chosen to mimic ViT feature spectra, and was scaled down for runtime; real all-layer concatenated features may be more or less stable.

No brain-subplane labels exist in this dataset, so 'what a code means' cannot be validated against fine-grained anatomy -- only against imaging plane, GA, and exemplar appearance. The finest available anatomical resolution is the 3-plane label, which is itself unreliable on the clinical set (audited 6/9 wrong-or-questionable, some at confidence 1.00).
Every faithfulness measure proposed here is internal to the representations; no clinician has assessed whether any code set is meaningful, and this track does not establish clinical interpretability.

The recommendation not to use a learned projection rests on a structural argument (the target is optimised) rather than on a measurement of collapse in this specific setting; a carefully regularised learned projection might avoid it, but a distilled student obtains the same benefit without the risk, so the argument was not pursued further.

Quantisation loses accuracy by construction (codes retain 82% of the GA clock, 0.385 vs 0.469). Nothing in this track improves that, and it should not be read as a cost of the recommended design -- it is inherent to having a discrete vocabulary at all.
I did not run any training or write training code, per the task constraint, so no claim here about student behaviour is empirical.
Interpretability.cost_estimate: Rank 1 null battery: days of CPU/analysis on features that already exist, NO training. The 1/E floor is closed-form; the encoder-shuffle floor is ~10-20 re-runs of codebook fitting on already-extracted features; per-encoder codebooks are 4 independent k-means/EMA fits; cross-vocabulary agreement needs subsampled RDMs (Mantel on ~1-5k patch subsamples, whole-fetus permutation, >=2000 permutations) which is minutes-to-hours on the existing 10-core/24GB local machine. Rank 2 raw-feature characterisation: one pass over the stored patch features per encoder to accumulate per-code sums and sums-of-squares -- I/O-bound, hours at most, no GPU. Rank 3 d=1024 robustness column: one extra projection plus codebook fit, ~4x the d=256 cost, still no training. Rank 4 distilled student (conditional, and only if Rank 1 clears the floor): this is the only expensive item -- a live 4-teacher forward pass is ~10 min/epoch on the single available GPU node, so a 50-100 epoch student run is roughly 8-17 GPU-hours, plus teacher-faithfulness evaluation and a full duplicate codebook analysis on the student substrate. Total if the null battery kills the framing: under a week of analysis and zero GPU. Total if it survives and the student is built: an additional ~1-2 days of GPU plus duplicated downstream analysis.

headline: ALL THREE tracks return viable-with-caveats, and all three recommend NOT replacing the fixed random projection: Interpretability says add nothing learned; Projection says a learned map is only safe if the reconstruction TARGET stays frozen raw features (break the target/projection coupling by construction, do NOT regularise your way out); Distillation says a student is a pre-registered CONTROL ARM, not a replacement.

CRITICAL FLAW FOUND IN THE DESIGN ALREADY RUN (1/E null floor): defining shared = arithmetic MEAN over E streams makes the mean carry exactly 1/E of the variance even when the TRUE shared fraction is ZERO. At E=4 encoders that is 25%; at E=3 depth groups it is 33%. Any 'shared explains ~25-30%' claim is inside the null. This floor was never subtracted in the depth-factorised result already reported (FULL 0.298 vs SHARED-ONLY 0.830) nor in the cross-encoder design. The fix is an encoder-shuffle / stream-shuffle floor run through the identical pipeline.

MIMIC EFFECT: cross-encoder agreement can be manufactured by a shared confound. Simulation at this project's parameters reached Mantel r=0.70 between encoders that were independent BY CONSTRUCTION. Imaging plane is the obvious culprit here (topic plane eta2 up to 0.78), so every agreement statistic must be recomputed WITHIN plane.
The fixed random projection was EXONERATED as the weak link: seed-stability decomposition attributes only +0.05-0.08 of instability to it, far less than the 1/E and mimic problems.

Distillation supervision budget is genuinely large (~956k target scalars per image vs 1 GA scalar), but the binding constraint is DIVERSITY not count: 20,413 frames is 686x fewer distinct images than DUNE (smallest agglomerative work) and 68,584x fewer than AM-RADIO, from one cohort and one 13-week GA window. No precedent exists for multi-teacher dense distillation at this scale with ultrasound teachers.

Joint student+VQ training is DISQUALIFIED by all tracks (matches the user's own instinct): a student trained alongside the codebook can collapse toward near-constant features that are trivially reconstructible - loss falls, representation empties.

Referent shift is the real cost of any learned component: after distillation the codebook describes the STUDENT's 20k-image four-teacher consensus, not the teachers and not fetal ultrasound. Random projection shares this in weaker form but is DATA-INDEPENDENT, so it cannot absorb cohort idiosyncrasy.
next_actions_ranked: 1. Run the 1/E / encoder-shuffle FLOOR on the features that already exist, BEFORE any further shared-vocabulary work. This is cheap and it decides whether there is a shared vocabulary to describe at all. It also retro-qualifies the already-reported depth-factorised shared/private split.
2. Recompute cross-encoder agreement WITHIN imaging plane (mimic-effect control).
3. Characterise codes by averaging RAW UNPROJECTED patch features per code per encoder (exact, fits nothing) - the sharpening the user asked for, with no learned component.
4. ONLY if 1-2 survive: the learned encoder-side map with FROZEN raw-feature targets, as one pre-registered primary comparison against the seeded random projection.
5. Distillation last, as a control arm, with RankMe effective-rank/dim >= 0.60 pass and < 0.30 kill on held-out patch tokens.
